title: Power Apps: model-driven apps as Business Applications in Work IQ
summary: The briefing passes: its controls, Dataverse calls, permissions and experience-dependent billing are supported. It accurately distinguishes the roadmap targets from published availability, reports conflicting Microsoft documentation, and qualifies default enablement and the remaining documentation gaps.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Direct Work IQ calls from coding agents or custom integrations are reported under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: **Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly**: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The Work IQ API consumption total can mix Microsoft 365 and business applications context rather than isolating Business Applications.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, the applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.
claims.quote: **Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat**: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.claim: A single request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so prompt cost varies.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Participation settings do not prevent agentic access; App Access controls application access to environment data.
claims.quote: App Access addresses application access to the underlying environment data. Work IQ participation settings serve a different purpose and don't prevent agentic access.

claims.claim: App participation is at Power Apps > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps.
claims.quote:
select **Apps**.
3. Find the app that you want to manage, and then select **Edit**.
4. On the app navigation bar, select **Settings**.
5. Select **Features**.
6. Set **Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps** to **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: POST <organization-url>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue with Content-Type: application/json accepts AppUniqueName, SettingName and Value for the m365copilotmodelappenabled app-setting override.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override. AppUniqueName | Edm.String | Model-driven app unique name (Optional). SettingName | Edm.String | Setting definition unique name (Required). Value | Edm.String | Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: App-level participation is a maker-managed setting.
claims.quote: Use the app-level setting to manage whether a model-driven app's tables, forms, and views are available in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research in Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Agent Builder. You need a maker account.

claims.claim: App setting changes require saving and publishing the app.
claims.quote: Select **Save** and then publish the app for the changes to take effect.

claims.claim: The maker configuration article labels the option Microsoft Copilot in model-driven apps.
claims.quote: To enable Microsoft Copilot, set **Microsoft Copilot in model-driven apps** to **On**. To disable it, set the option to **Off**.

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ MCP tenant policy
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy documentation describes mutation operations as disallowed by default for Microsoft 365 resource access.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ MCP tenant policy
claims.claim: Whether that default mutation policy also governs Business Applications writes remains unconfirmed in the checked documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications" "Work IQ" "mutation" policy. Opened policy-governance-mcp, manage-participation and add-work-iq. Policy text covers Microsoft 365 resources; no passage explicitly states its default for Business Applications writes.
